# deadnix

Scan `.nix` files for dead code (unused variable bindings).

## Usage with Github Actions

See [deadnix-action](https://github.com/astro/deadnix-action)


## Usage with Nix Flakes

### Help

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix -- --help
Find dead code in .nix files

Usage: deadnix [OPTIONS] [FILE_PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [FILE_PATHS]...  .nix files, or directories with .nix files inside [default: .]

Options:
  -l, --no-lambda-arg                  Don't check lambda parameter arguments
  -L, --no-lambda-pattern-names        Don't check lambda attrset pattern names (don't break nixpkgs callPackage)
  -_, --no-underscore                  Don't check any bindings that start with a _
  -q, --quiet                          Don't print dead code report
  -e, --edit                           Remove unused code and write to source file
  -h, --hidden                         Recurse into hidden subdirectories and process hidden .*.nix files
      --help
  -f, --fail                           Exit with 1 if unused code has been found
  -o, --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>  Output format to use [default: human-readable] [possible values: human-readable, json]
      --exclude <EXCLUDES>...          Files to exclude from analysis
  -V, --version                        Print version
```

Reports contain ANSI color escape codes unless the
[`$NO_COLOR`](https://no-color.org/) environment variable is set.

The `--exclude` parameter accepts multiple paths. Separate them with
`--` to pass `[FILE_PATHS]...`.

### Scan for unused code

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix example.nix
Warning: Unused declarations were found.
    ╭─[example.nix:1:1]
  1 │unusedArgs@{ unusedArg, usedArg, ... }:
    ·     │           ╰───── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArg
    ·     ╰───────────────── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArgs
  3 │  inherit (builtins) unused_inherit;
    ·                            ╰─────── Unused let binding: unused_inherit
  5 │  unused = "fnord";
    ·     ╰─── Unused let binding: unused
 10 │  shadowed = 42;
    ·      ╰──── Unused let binding: shadowed
 11 │  _unused = unused: false;
    ·     │         ╰─── Unused lambda argument: unused
    ·     ╰───────────── Unused let binding: _unused
 13 │  x = { unusedArg2, x ? args.y, ... }@args: used1 + x;
    ·             ╰───── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArg2
```


### Remove unused code automatically

**Do commit** your changes into version control **before!**

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix -- -eq test.nix
```

## Usage with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/)

Add the following to your project's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astro/deadnix
    rev: ID # frozen: VERSION
    hooks:
      - id: deadnix
        #args: [--edit] # Uncomment to automatically modify files
        stages: [commit]
```

Replace `ID` and `VERSION` above with the relevant version tag and
commit ID for reference, for example:

```yaml
rev: da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709  # frozen: v1.2.3
```

## Behavior

### Renaming of all unused to lambda args to start with `_`

If you disfavor marking them as unused, use option
`-l`/`--no-lambda-arg`.


### nixpkgs `callPackages` with multiple imports

`callPackages` guesses the packages to inject by the names of a
packages' lambda attrset pattern names. Some packages alias these with
`@args` to pass them to another `import ...nix args`.

As the used args are only named in the imported file they will be
recognized as dead in the package source file that is imported by
`callPackage`, rendering it unable to guess the dependencies to call
the packages with.

Use option `-L`/`--no-lambda-pattern-names` in this case.


### Skipping reports for certain declarations

As of 1.1.0 deadnix supports the following pragma to skip check of
bindings in the following line:

```nix
# deadnix: skip
```


## What if the produced reports are wrong?

Please open an issue. Do not forget to include the `.nix` code that
produces incorrect results.


## Commercial Support

The author can be hired to implement the features that you wish, or to
integrate this tool into your toolchain.

def scan(code, extra=None):
    open("/tmp/t.nix","w").write(code)

    # Actually need NO_COLOR but json no colors

    if extra:
        cmd=[EXE]+extra+["/tmp/t.nix"]

        cmd=[EXE,"-o","json","/tmp/t.nix"]
    r=subprocess.run(cmd,capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)
    try:
        j=json.loads(r.stdout.strip()) if r.stdout.strip() else None
    except: j=r.stdout
    return r, j

tests=[
 ("let unused, simple", 'let x = 1; in 2\n'),
 ("let used", 'let x = 1; in x\n'),
 ("let rec mutual", 'let a = b; b = 1; in a\n'),
 ("let shadowing", 'let x = 1; in let x = 2; in x\n'),
 ("let shadow outer unused?", 'let x = 1; in let x = 2; in x\n'), # outer x unused? but shadowed?
 ("lambda arg unused", 'x: 1\n'),
 ("lambda arg used", 'x: x\n'),
 ("lambda pattern unused", '{ a, b }: b\n'),
 ("lambda pattern with @", 'args@{ a, b }: b\n'),
 ("lambda pattern @ only unused?", 'args@{ a, b }: a\n'), # args unused?
 ("inherit", 'let inherit (builtins) toString; in toString 1\n'),
 ("rec set", 'rec { a = 1; b = a; }\n'),
 ("with?", 'with builtins; toString 1\n'),
 ("attrset", '{ a = 1; b = 2; }\n'),
 ("dynamic key", 'let x = 1; in { "${x}" = 2; }\n'),
]
for name, code in tests:
    r,j=scan(code)
    print(f"TEST {name}: code={repr(code)}")
    print(f"  => {j}")

]:

    print(f"{repr(line)} => {res}")

 '"# deadnix: skip"\nlet x = 1; in 2\n', # string literal file? invalid? Actually file starting with string then let? invalid.
]:
    r,j=scan(code)

 'let x = 1; x = 2; in 1\n',

]:
    r,j=scan(code)

# deadnix

Scan `.nix` files for dead code (unused variable bindings).

## Usage with Github Actions

See [deadnix-action](https://github.com/astro/deadnix-action)


## Usage with Nix Flakes

### Help

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix -- --help
Find dead code in .nix files

Usage: deadnix [OPTIONS] [FILE_PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [FILE_PATHS]...  .nix files, or directories with .nix files inside [default: .]

Options:
  -l, --no-lambda-arg                  Don't check lambda parameter arguments
  -L, --no-lambda-pattern-names        Don't check lambda attrset pattern names (don't break nixpkgs callPackage)
  -_, --no-underscore                  Don't check any bindings that start with a _
  -q, --quiet                          Don't print dead code report
  -e, --edit                           Remove unused code and write to source file
  -h, --hidden                         Recurse into hidden subdirectories and process hidden .*.nix files
      --help
  -f, --fail                           Exit with 1 if unused code has been found
  -o, --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>  Output format to use [default: human-readable] [possible values: human-readable, json]
      --exclude <EXCLUDES>...          Files to exclude from analysis
  -V, --version                        Print version
```

Reports contain ANSI color escape codes unless the
[`$NO_COLOR`](https://no-color.org/) environment variable is set.

The `--exclude` parameter accepts multiple paths. Separate them with
`--` to pass `[FILE_PATHS]...`.

### Scan for unused code

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix example.nix
Warning: Unused declarations were found.
    ╭─[example.nix:1:1]
  1 │unusedArgs@{ unusedArg, usedArg, ... }:
    ·     │           ╰───── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArg
    ·     ╰───────────────── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArgs
  3 │  inherit (builtins) unused_inherit;
    ·                            ╰─────── Unused let binding: unused_inherit
  5 │  unused = "fnord";
    ·     ╰─── Unused let binding: unused
 10 │  shadowed = 42;
    ·      ╰──── Unused let binding: shadowed
 11 │  _unused = unused: false;
    ·     │         ╰─── Unused lambda argument: unused
    ·     ╰───────────── Unused let binding: _unused
 13 │  x = { unusedArg2, x ? args.y, ... }@args: used1 + x;
    ·             ╰───── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArg2
```


### Remove unused code automatically

**Do commit** your changes into version control **before!**

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix -- -eq test.nix
```

## Usage with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/)

Add the following to your project's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astro/deadnix
    rev: ID # frozen: VERSION
    hooks:
      - id: deadnix
        #args: [--edit] # Uncomment to automatically modify files
        stages: [commit]
```

Replace `ID` and `VERSION` above with the relevant version tag and
commit ID for reference, for example:

```yaml
rev: da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709  # frozen: v1.2.3
```

## Behavior

### Renaming of all unused to lambda args to start with `_`

If you disfavor marking them as unused, use option
`-l`/`--no-lambda-arg`.

import subprocess, os

def run(args, env_extra=None, cwd="/workspace"):
    env=dict(os.environ)
    # clear NO_COLOR for some?
    if env_extra:
        for k,v in env_extra.items():
            if v is None:
                env.pop(k,None)
            else:
                env[k]=v
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,env=env,cwd=cwd)
    return r

# NO_COLOR variations
for env in [{}, {"NO_COLOR":"1"}, {"NO_COLOR":""}, {"NO_COLOR":"0"}]:
    # need to ensure base env has NO_COLOR removed for first case
    base=dict(os.environ)
    base.pop("NO_COLOR",None)
    base.update({k:v for k,v in env.items()})
    # for empty case, need to handle?
    r=subprocess.run([EXE,"example.nix"],capture_output=True,text=True,env=base,cwd="/workspace")
    has_color="\x1b[" in r.stdout
    print(f"env={env} has_color={has_color} out_start={repr(r.stdout[:100])}")

# test combined short flags
for a in [["-lq","example.nix"], ["-ql","example.nix"], ["-lL","example.nix"], ["-Wq","example.nix"], ["-_q","example.nix"]]:
    r=run(a, {"NO_COLOR":"1"})
    print(f"{a} exit={r.returncode} out_len={len(r.stdout)} err={repr(r.stderr[:100])}")

# test -o with = ?
for a in [["--output-format=json","example.nix"], ["-o=json","example.nix"], ["--exclude=/tmp/foo","--","example.nix"]]:

# test stdin? 
for a in [["-"], [["/dev/stdin"]]]:
    pass

  -W, --warn-used-underscore           Warn if bindings are referenced that start with '_'

  -e, --edit                           Remove unused code and write to source file
  -h, --hidden                         Recurse into hidden subdirectories and process hidden .*.nix files

  -V, --version                        Print version
"""

    def parse_lambda(self):
        # Assumes is_lambda_start true. Need to handle two forms:
        #  ident [: @ ...] : body  OR  { formals } [@ident] : body  OR ident@{ formals } : body (which is ident @ { ... } : )
        # Actually forms:  args@{ a, b }: ..., { a, b }@args: ..., args: ..., { a }: ...
        # So header can be: [ident @] { formals } [@ident] :  OR ident :  (with optional @? No, ident: has no @, ident@{...}: has @)
        # Simplify: parse header left to right.
        self.skip_ws_comments()
        # Check for { first?
        if self.pos < self.n and self.src[self.pos] == '{':
            # { formals } [@ident] :
            formals = self.parse_formals()
            # formals is list of (name, s, e, default_range or None)
            # Check for @
            self.skip_ws_comments()
            at_alias = None
            at_s = at_e = None
            if self.pos < self.n and self.src[self.pos] == '@':
                self.pos += 1
                self.skip_ws_comments()
                r = self.parse_ident_raw()
                if r is None:
                    self.error("unexpected token, wanted identifier after @")
                    # try to recover?
                    return
                at_alias, at_s, at_e = r
            # expect :
            self.skip_ws_comments()
            if self.pos < self.n and self.src[self.pos] == ':':
                self.pos += 1
            else:
                self.error("unexpected token, wanted ':'")
                return
            # Now we have formals + at_alias. Need to create bindings and push scope, then parse defaults and body.
            # Collect all names for scope
            scope_dict = {}
            bindings_for_scope = []
            # formals
            for (nm, s, e, dflt) in formals:
                line, col, end_col = self.span_line_col(s, e)
                b = Binding(nm, line, col, end_col, 'lambda_pattern', s, e, is_at_alias=False, is_inner=True)
                self.bindings.append(b)
                bindings_for_scope.append(b)
                scope_dict.setdefault(nm, []).append(b)
            # at_alias
